absent: Exact numeric values of fine grained mask tables and trap bit positions.
Full memory layouts of vcpu, cpu context, mask, location and reserved-bit records beyond observed fields.
Concurrency rules for VM wide trap desires and ID tables beyond local interrupt and preemption handling shown.
Semantics of EL1, EL2 and 32 bit restore helpers, partitioning load, stage two load and guest ownership predicates referenced but not routed.
Put and unload paths that reverse the load, save and trap installation sequences.

findings.text: kvm_vcpu_load_fgt refreshes cached fine grained trap controls for a vcpu. It does nothing without the main trap capability, otherwise it refreshes general plus debug plus AMU groups, then second generation groups when that capability exists and interrupt controller groups when the GICv5 interface exists.

Per register trap value starts from the mask default deny set, merges VM wide desired bits split by allow versus deny masks, additionally merges nested hypervisor requests when in nested context including inverted deny handling, then forces reserved one bits and clears reserved zero bits before storing into the vcpu cache.

Each fine grained trap control resolves to a dedicated mask record holding allow, deny, reserved one and reserved zero components. The mapping covers general, debug, AMU, second generation and interrupt controller controls, with an unreachable default that fails the build.

After generic computation, general write traps gain an extra trap on affected Ampere parts, debug write traps gain a debug control trap in hypervisor context, interrupt read traps force trapping of affinity and identity registers to hide host features, and interrupt write traps force trapping of PPI enabler writes while leaving reads untrapped.

kvm_vcpu_load_debug must run before the VHE load and requires system registers not already marked on CPU. It preserves host debug control on VHE, selects host owned debug when userspace debugging or OS lock is active, otherwise guest owned versus free from guest enables, adjusts single step pending state, then programs debug trap control.

Debug ownership has three states: host owned when the host needs breakpoint, watchpoint or single step resources or must emulate OS lock, guest owned when the guest enabled debug exceptions and needs eager loading, and free when neither applies. The state is recomputed on every vcpu load from guest requests, lock state and guest control bits.

Debug trap control starts with host counter count encoded in the reserved counter field and with profiling, trace and debug memory trapped. Userspace debugging routes software debug to the hypervisor, lack of guest ownership traps debug registers, nested state may add guest bits, and on VHE the value is written immediately to hardware.

Nested debug control merges only an allowed subset of guest requested bits when in nested context. Outside nested context without fine grained trap support it conservatively forces debug register trapping to cover redirected debug control effects.

Host used debug control derives from the guest value with single step and global enables cleared, then re enables single step for userspace single step requests and global debug for hardware breakpoint use. Clearing the main enable also satisfies OS lock emulation.

vcpu_read_sys_reg returns the current architectural view of a register by first locating where the value lives. Special timer and control identifiers use dedicated handling, currently loaded registers are read from hardware unless translation is required, sanitised identifiers get reserved bit correction, and other cases fall back to memory.

When registers are not marked on CPU every access resolves to memory. When marked, hypervisor registers with guest aliases map through a helper that stays in memory outside hypervisor context and becomes loaded plus mapped inside it with optional translation when extended mode is off, two timer and control registers have extra special handling, NVHCR self maps in nested guests, and the rest use direct rules.

Direct location treats guest registers that have hypervisor aliases as loaded only outside hypervisor context, treats thread pointers and a small always available set as always loaded, and treats non mapped hypervisor registers as always in memory.

Hardware reads use EL12 aliases for the guest set, direct reads for thread pointers and always loaded state, and dedicated hypervisor encodings for 32 bit debug and nested control, with a sentinel initial value and a one time warning for unexpected identifiers.
Sanitised values are normalised by clearing VM specific reserved zero bits and setting reserved one bits obtained from a per VM table keyed by register identifier.

Floating point load requires process context and does nothing without host vector support. Transitions between nested levels skip host save under an assumption of non preemptible context with host state already unbound and verify the host does not own registers, otherwise it saves host state, marks ownership free and verifies streaming state is clear when SME exists.
VHE vcpu load records the running vcpu in host data, switches system register state, activates trap controls and loads stage two translation state.
Common trap activation runs with local interrupts saved and restored around the update, while debug trap programming runs with preemption disabled across construction and optional hardware write.

Common activation traps legacy 32 bit implementation defined accesses, sanitises performance monitor selection and user enable state while marking it on CPU, saves and installs extended control with nested guest bits merged through an exclusion mask when nested, then delegates to fine grained, interrupt controller and partitioning helpers.

Fine grained activation does nothing without the main capability, otherwise it saves host values and installs cached guest values for general and debug groups, includes the AMU group only when the CPU reports that feature, and includes second generation groups only when present. Interrupt groups are handled separately and gated on the GICv5 interface.

Partitioning trap setup does nothing without that feature, otherwise it disables secure monitoring while trapping guest accesses to partitioning controls and identity registers, using either a dedicated hypervisor control or a fallback trap bit depending on hardware support.

Register switching saves host user thread state, issues a barrier for nested capable VMs to complete speculative walks, restores 32 bit state before system registers, restores user and partitioning state, then restores either virtual EL2 state in hypervisor context or EL1 state otherwise using virtual identifiers for nested guests and real identifiers otherwise, finally marking registers on CPU.

Guest identification returns hardware identity unless the VM allows writable ID registers, in which case the VM table value is used. Context to vcpu resolution prefers the recorded running vcpu and falls back to container lookup, guest detection compares against the host pointer, and user save preserves both thread pointers.

Observed state includes per VM desired trap bits and mask records with allow, deny and reserved components, per vcpu cached traps plus debug ownership, trap control and external debug control, host saved debug and trap state with counter count and vector owner, and CPU context register storage with a running vcpu link.

Loading debug after registers are marked on CPU, loading vector state without process context or with host ownership during nested transitions, and reading translated registers from CPU instead of memory can corrupt state; affected paths assert or warn rather than recovering.

Capability identifiers gate fine grained traps, second generation traps, GICv5 interface, extended control, AMU, partitioning, nested variants and VHE behavior, while flag identifiers track registers on CPU, guest and host single step pending, user enable on CPU and nested transition states.
